stories.title: Fed's Goolsbee Says Inflation Is Moving the Wrong Way as Hike Bets Firm

photo.alt: The Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago building with a U.S. flag; file photo.

paragraphs: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said Friday the central bank has work to do to restore its credibility on inflation. He told CNBC inflation is rising and starting to spread. He spoke after new wholesale price data.

The producer price index rose 0.3% in October, slightly below forecasts. CNBC reports it was up 6.5% from a year earlier, the biggest annual gain since November 2022. The 10-year Treasury yield rose to about 5.14%.
Goolsbee pointed to demand from the AI data center buildout as a new source of pressure. He said the Fed is not on a path back to its 2% target. He is not a voter on rates this year.

Why it matters. Higher rates raise costs for mortgages, car loans and credit cards. Traders now price a 100% chance of a hike at the Dec. 9 meeting, according to CME Group's FedWatch. CNBC puts the odds of a half-point move at about 14%.

stories.title: Duffy Seeks $50 Billion After Aging Air Traffic Gear Halts US Flights

photo.alt: Departure boards above empty check-in desks at a Spanish airport; file photo.

paragraphs: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy wants about $50 billion to overhaul air traffic control after old equipment forced a nationwide halt to departures Friday. BBC News reports it was the longest nationwide ground stop since the Sept. 11 attacks. It lasted more than four hours.

Duffy said airspace reopened at 8:15 p.m. ET Friday. CNBC reports more than 3,000 U.S. flights were canceled Saturday as of 5:45 a.m. ET, citing FlightAware. More than 3,500 planes were in the air when the order came.

Duffy said overloaded routers in an old system gave inconsistent data, so officials shut it down. Al Jazeera reports officials said new technology added to the system overloaded older parts. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no sign of a cyberattack.

Why it matters. Duffy warned the old system is going to continue to fail. Al Jazeera reports he expects operations to be back in time for the Thanksgiving travel rush. Duffy said the effects could ripple for a few days.

stories.title: Bessent Says Agencies Sought Curbs on a Firm Tied to the Nvidia Scandal

photo.alt: Close-up of a dark blue printed circuit board; illustrative file photo.

paragraphs: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Friday that several agencies wanted export curbs on Megaspeed for months. He told CNBC the Commerce Department is in charge of that decision. Megaspeed is at the center of the scandal that ended Jensen Huang's run as Nvidia chief.

Bessent said Treasury, Defense, State and the trade representative's office all backed adding Megaspeed to the entity list. He said leakage of advanced chips to China hurts U.S. companies. Commerce had earlier denied a reported clash between Bessent and Secretary Howard Lutnick.

Bessent said the real question is whether Nvidia knew its client. NBC News reports a senior U.S. official said the Nvidia case should have no bearing on Trump's coming China trip. The official said export controls are not up for negotiation.

Why it matters. The dispute exposes a rift inside the administration over chip policy. Commerce said Lutnick has agreed to appear voluntarily before the Senate Banking Committee. Commerce did not respond to CNBC about Bessent's remarks.

stories.title: Qatar and Turkiye Sign a Mutual Defense Pact as Gulf Tensions Persist

photo.alt: A ferry crosses the Bosphorus below mosques in Istanbul; file photo.

paragraphs: Qatar and Turkiye have agreed to a mutual defense pact against any outside armed attack on either country. Al Jazeera reports it followed a meeting in Istanbul on Friday. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Qatar's emir chaired the talks.

The two countries will consult on threats and expand joint drills, arms production and training. The joint communique did not say what would trigger the pact or how they would respond. An analyst at Qatar University said it is meant to deter, not to target a country.

The deal comes as the region deals with fallout from the U.S. and Israeli war on Iran. Al Jazeera's live coverage reports it also comes amid disruption to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Al Jazeera reports the communique also welcomed a defense memorandum signed by Turkiye, Qatar, Pakistan and Indonesia.
Why it matters. Gulf states are seeking new security ties and less reliance on outside powers. Ankara and Doha called for the swift and full reopening of safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz.

deep_dive.title: What to Expect When Trump, Xi and Putin Meet in Shenzhen

photo.alt: Shenzhen's Houhai skyline reflected in the bay at dusk; file photo.

paragraphs: President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin plan a first three-way meeting next week. NBC News reports it will take place on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen. The White House announced it Friday night.

What happened. A White House spokesperson said Trump will discuss reducing nuclear weapons. A senior U.S. official said no agreement is expected and called it a first conversation. Trump also plans to raise the Iran war. A senior official said Ukraine is on a separate track and will not be discussed.

The backstory. Al Jazeera reports the last U.S. and Russian nuclear arms treaty, New START, expired in February. Trump then sought a new deal that includes China. NBC News cites Pentagon estimates that China has more than 600 warheads. The U.S. and Russia each have more than 5,000.

What comes next. The Guardian reports Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is among those who fear a Yalta-style carve-up. Al Jazeera reports the Kremlin dismissed that comparison but called the meeting extremely significant. The Guardian reports China is already trying to push nuclear disarmament off the agenda. NBC News reports no separate one-on-one meeting with Putin is scheduled. Elon Musk will travel with Trump but skip the official meetings.

World view: Siege deepens disease fears in Taiz. Health officials logged 5,642 disease cases in four weeks as a Houthi siege cuts off supplies; Al Jazeera reports.
Europe names its Ukraine talks team. The EU and five countries, including the UK, France and Germany, will represent Europe at the next round of peace talks; Al Jazeera reports.
Need to know: Alaska picks its youngest governor. Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, 37, flips the office from Republicans in a projected win; NBC News reports.
Hassett denies he is leaving. The National Economic Council director called a report of his planned exit not true; CNBC reports.
Money & markets: Apple hits a record high. Shares reached an intraday record of $360.80 on Friday as investors moved away from AI infrastructure names; CNBC reports.
Chip rivals rally on Nvidia turmoil. AMD and Broadcom are up about 17% over the past week, and Nvidia reports earnings Nov. 17; CNBC reports.
Future frontiers: Starship booster catch called off. SpaceX sent its booster into the ocean Friday and will decide Saturday whether to try catching the upper stage; BBC News reports.
A blood test speeds cancer matching. A Manchester lab cut results for a gene test that guides targeted lung and breast cancer drugs to 14 days; BBC News reports.
The score: Pochettino leaves the U.S. team. The coach became Manchester United's head coach and will lead the U.S. against Haiti on Nov. 14 and 18 first; BBC Sport reports.
Ground stop scrambles college football travel. Purdue took buses to Iowa and Auburn bused to Mississippi State, where the SEC pushed back kickoff; NBC News reports.
Life & culture: A new Bond draws near. Amazon MGM Studios is preparing to name the next 007, with five actors widely seen as the shortlist; The Guardian reports.
Darth Vader's lightsaber sells for $4.875 million. The prop from The Empire Strikes Back set a record for an on-screen Star Wars item; The Guardian reports.

uncertainties: Flight counts are FlightAware via CNBC as of 5:45 a.m. ET Saturday; they will rise during the day.
Fed hike odds are Friday CNBC/CME levels, pre-weekend.
Summit details come from the White House and anonymous senior U.S. officials; no date beyond next week is stated.
Starship upper-stage catch decision is due about 21:15 GMT Saturday, after delivery; copy states only the plan.
Bond shortlist is press understanding, not an announcement.
